subject: Frailty survival model  - Regions with no data

messages.author: a259015b36a46546
messages.subject: Frailty survival model  - Regions with no data
parts:
Dear all,

I am running a survival model with cases nested in regions. The definition of my cohort means some regions in the study country has no information for both the outcome and covariates. Approximately half of the 2210 regions has no data however i wanted to get estimates for the regions with no data. 

I defined my formula as 

form <- inla.surv(time, outcome) + 1 + x1 ... + xn + f(ID, model="iid")

I want to know if the estimates from the regions with no data would be reliable considering it is an iid model or should I use bym model instead of the former (iid). 

Thank you.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Frailty survival model  - Regions with no data
parts:
the iid model might be correct, but you only transfer the precision for
the random effect from its neighbours. If you think that random effect
have some spatial pattern, then you might want to consider a different
model (like some regional model often used for disease mapping)
